title: How to choose laminates for kitchens and wardrobes
excerpt: Finish, thickness and placement all matter. A short guide to choosing laminates that look good and last.
author: Comfort Nest Team

content.text: Laminates are the most common finish on modern furniture. They come in hundreds of designs, but a few practical choices decide how well they age.

Standard decorative laminates are around 1 mm thick and suit most shutters and carcass faces. Thinner 0.8 mm sheets are often used for internal surfaces or vertical use, while thicker grades are used where more impact resistance is needed, such as worktops or high-traffic tables.

items: Matte: hides smudges, calm look, good for everyday wardrobes
Suede: soft touch and low glare, resists fingerprints
Gloss and acrylic: reflective and bright, but show marks and need regular wiping
Textured and woodgrain: add depth and hide minor scratches

content.text: Choose easy-to-clean finishes for shutters. Keep laminates away from continuous heat and steam, and use edge banding that is sealed properly. Remember that the laminate is only the surface: the board underneath should be BWP or a similar moisture-resistant core.

Matte or suede finishes work well because hands touch the shutters often. Use a lighter colour inside to make clothes easier to find, and consider a balancing laminate on the back of large shutters so they stay flat.

items: Look at full sheets or large samples in your home's light, not just small chips
Match edge banding to the face colour
Ask which adhesive and pressing method the carpenter uses
Order all sheets together so shades match
